question.text: Orchid Buyout Fund II (Cat II) is appointing an independent valuer for quarterly fair-value assessment of its unlisted portfolio companies. Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the minimum experience the independent valuer must have in valuation of unlisted securities?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, independent valuers appointed by AIF Managers must have a minimum of 3 years of experience in valuation of unlisted securities. This ensures that the valuer has seen at least one market cycle and has meaningful track record in the illiquid-asset valuation space. **The Trap:** 1 year understates. 5 years is the sponsor eligibility track record for some products — not the valuer requirement. 10 years is excessive. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same 3-year rule. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) has different valuation norms (PMS values listed daily, no equivalent valuer registration). IBBI Registered Valuer rules apply in Companies Act contexts — different track. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Rotate valuers every few fund cycles — LPs view long-tenure incumbents as a soft-conflict risk. Also: check whether your valuer is APMI-empanelled (AIF and PMS Industry body) — most large LP diligence packs now ask for APMI empanelment as a baseline.
